minutes.headline: Committee reorganized, kept its committee assignments, and agreed academic programs outrank housing TCP programs.
minutes.summary: The committee reorganized, electing its chair, vice chair and secretary, and approved committee assignments, school handbooks, school improvement plans and the FY23 meeting calendar. It discussed digitizing records, shortening meetings and the future of programs housed at TC Passios. Two residents spoke about a candlelight vigil.

public_comment.topic: Announced a candlelight vigil to stop violence on June 10 in front of the TC Passios building, pending Select Board approval, and asked for help involving students.
Supported the vigil and asked for the committee's input.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call, three yes heard, chair accepted)

votes.motion: Continue all existing policies for the ensuing year
Authorize student activity funds for the four schools
Waiver allowing food and beverages with lids in the auditorium for town meetings
Approve the school committee meeting calendar
Go into executive session and adjourn afterward

budget_items.what_was_said: Committee authorized student activity funds for the primary, Turkey Hill, middle and high schools.
A late June meeting was added so the committee can approve purchase orders carried over past fiscal year end.
A member recalled the town figure for digitizing records, and another noted it was in the capital plan; schools to investigate cost and a multi-year plan.
The superintendent said recommendations on TCP programs assumed the school budget would stay within annual growth and not require program cuts.
Giving extended day gym access would end youth basketball rentals and lose revenue.
The superintendent said ESSER money funded positions and that reporting on its use was required.

decisions.decision: No line item transfers this evening.
Class of 2022 scoreboard donation passed over until the figure is known.
Administration to investigate records digitizing costs and a possible capital plan request.
Next meeting will aim for about two and a half hours; no formal vote.
Committee agreed informally that academic programs take priority over TCP programs and no leases.
Meeting protocols to be reviewed at the first fall meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee reorganized, electing a chair, vice chair and secretary by roll call, and continued all existing policies.
The committee approved its appointments and assignments, the 2022-2023 school handbooks and the meeting calendar, each on a four-yes roll call.
The committee accepted the school improvement plans on a four-yes roll call.
Members agreed informally, without a vote, that academic programs take priority over programs housed at TC Passios and over leases.
Administration was asked to investigate the cost of digitizing records and a possible capital plan request.

why_it_matters: The informal priority for academic programs over TC Passios programs and leases signals how the building's future use may be weighed, though nothing was voted and no lease decision was made.
The superintendent's TC Passios recommendations assumed the school budget would stay within annual growth, so program choices there are tied to how much the budget is allowed to rise.
Records digitizing could become a capital plan request, which would be a spending item residents may later be asked to vote on.
watch_next: A late June meeting was added so the committee can approve purchase orders carried over past fiscal year end.
Meeting protocols are to be reviewed at the first fall meeting.
